name: Diegetic object wipe

source.description: An inspected reference (batch 1, 2026-11-26) closes an eyelid across a macro eye to carry the cut to black; a film-editing convention (doors, passing objects, page turns).

technique: Something that belongs to the scene (an eyelid, a page, a door, a card, a hand) moves across the frame and becomes the matte for the cut, so the transition is part of the story instead of an effect laid on top.
purpose: Motivated transition that also says something (the viewer blinks, a page turns, a door closes on a chapter).
visual_behaviour: The object closes over the frame in 0.3-0.6 s; the next scene is revealed when it opens again, or appears on the object's colour.
mechanics: Draw the object as an SVG shape in the overlay layer (two lids, a page, a panel); animate its path or transform to full cover with power2.in; swap scenes under full cover; reopen with power2.out or cut to the next scene on the object's colour. Eyelid: two curved paths meeting at the horizon line, lashes as strokes.

decomposition.timing: Close 0.3-0.6 s; hold 0-0.3 s; open 0.3-0.5 s.

parameters.name: object
parameters.description: eyelid, page, door, panel or a custom SVG path pair

parameters.name: reopen
parameters.description: Reopen onto the next scene (true) or cut on the cover colour (false)

failure_modes: An object that does not belong to the scene reads as a generic wipe
Lid or page edges with hard straight lines look mechanical; curve and soften them
Too slow a close kills momentum

implementation.approach: Studio.fx.shapeCover with a custom SVG path for the covering shape, or a pair of lid paths tweened with attr d (same point count) in the overlay layer; scenes swap under cover.

provenance.observed: Eyelashes close down across a macro eye and the frame goes black; the closing line then types and slams onto that black.

licensing_notes: Technique only (film convention plus a user-supplied reference, inspiration-only, rights unknown).
